jobs.name: Bổ dọc – Trấn Sơn
jobs.motion: Option1 VERTICAL OVERHEAD DROP. Four phases: 1 gather the hammer tightly across the waist and sink into hips; 2 extend BOTH hands and the ENTIRE haft high ABOVE the crown, elbows opening, hammer iron head clearly above all hair, back slightly arched; 3 one short forward step/stomp and full torso hinge drive the head down onto the floor directly IN FRONT at screen-right, deep compressed knees and shoulders, both hands still on shaft; 4 hold the grounded low finish briefly, then begin lifting the head to return. A strongly vertical top-to-bottom trajectory, minimal lateral rotation. Emphasize very HIGH overhead loading contrasted with LOW ground contact; an understated ground dust accent only at phase3 is allowed. This should feel planted, monumental and deliberate.

Keep the head/torso size, shaft length and hammer head rigid and consistent in every pose. Four large complete figures from left to right on a clean dark charcoal-grey art-director board, all facing screen right/front-right from a FIXED elevated orthographic three-quarter camera. Separate poses clearly with a subtle thin curved gold trajectory arrow illustrating the mallet head's actual path; keep character hands and shaft unobscured. Solo martial movement study: no opponents, injury, blood or broken scenery. jobs.name: Quật chéo – Phá Nhạc
jobs.motion: Option2 DIAGONAL SHOULDER/HIP SWING, clearly different from a vertical overhead drop. Four phases: 1 bring the hammer beside the rear shoulder, head behind/above that shoulder, both hands spaced on the haft; 2 coil hips and chest together with a bent rear knee, weapon head well behind the torso, ready to transfer weight; 3 step into a broad DIAGONAL arc from high-back to low-front, rotate hips and chest powerfully together and place the head on the floor in front-right, maintaining the two-hand grip; 4 finish across the front of the body, chest rotated and weight over the front leg, heel and hammer settled. Show the sweeping diagonal silhouette and visible torso twist; NOT a horizontal waist-level sweep and NOT simply lifting straight overhead. A faint dusty crescent at floor contact is allowed.

jobs.name: Hất ngược – Bạt Sơn
jobs.motion: Option3 LOW-TO-HIGH SCOOP, clearly different from the two downward motions. Four phases: 1 lower hammer head near the front knee/ground while keeping both hands on the shaft; 2 sit deeply into hips and bring the head slightly back along the floor-side of the body, spine braced and rear leg loaded; 3 extend legs and hips upward to guide the hammer head in a forceful RISING arc from low-front to high-front, still with both hands on the shaft and BOTH feet grounded; 4 finish with head at upper chest/shoulder height in front of him, arms bent rather than stretched overhead, then prepare to lower back to guard. Make the unmistakable upward path clear with the trajectory arrow. This is an upward lever powered by legs/hips, not an overhead drop, jump, hammer toss or one-arm lifting pose. No floor-explosion accent because the emphasis is the upward motion.
